newsitem.title: POLAND: Early zloty steadies around c.bank support.
newsitem.headline: Early zloty steadies around c.bank support.

text.p: The Polish zloty stabilised around expected central bank support levels at 3.5 percent below the parity rate early on Monday with no foreign orders to stir up trade so far, dealers said.

Dealers said that any prolonged zloty weakening past 3.5 percent below parity would probably be met with National Bank of Poland currency selling interventions, after the NBP sold some $50 million on Friday to stop the zloty's decline.
"The market is waiting for NBP action if the zloty weakens but bids have so far remained around support," one forex dealer from a large Polish bank said.
At 0850 GMT the zloty was at -3.48/-3.63 percent from parity against -3.49/-3.89 percent at 0715 GMT.
It was at 3.4855/05 to the dollar, against 3.4850/950 at opening and at 1.9445/75 to the mark, against 1.9450/550.
Dealers said any zloty gains on the back of NBP action would be limited by foreign investor sales of Polish treasuries taking advantage of more favourable exchange rates.

Dealers expected the NBP to raise official interest rates soon to cool credit action and offset additional government borrowing needed to finance relief of a weeks-long flood, which swamped more than one percent of Poland underwater.
On the money market one-day rates held flat as Monday's large 710 million zloty inflow created some short-term liquidity on the market, dealers said.
At 0900 GMT overnight rates were at 23.38/23.85 percent against opening's 23.60/23.75. Tomorrow/next were at 23.48/23.90 percent against 23.80/24.00 at 0655 GMT.
Dealers said interest rate rise expectations pushed up two- and three-month deposits to around the 25 percent lombard rate.
At 0905 GMT three month depos were quoted at 23.85/25.00 percent. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
